response.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, stable termination, and cross-wrapper reachability. Key findings: (1) the root-level initial edge [*]->HumanDriving (transition:line:19, triggered by Power_On) is unreachable_from_initial=false per inspection-equivalent facts and verify_facts refutes its initial-entry check, so NL3's initial_entry contract (root -> HumanDriving on power on) is violated because the exact required owner-local edge is present syntactically but is not the reachable/effective entry (the effective unconditional entry into the composite root at line 2/... is actually via the same [*]->HumanDriving edge - checking more closely: state_refs show root machine state is llms_emp_feedback_final_0040 which is itself reachable_from_initial=true with no incoming edge info, and the [*]->HumanDriving transition (line 19) is marked reachable_from_initial=false while HumanDriving itself is reachable_from_initial=true via a different path). Given the diagnostic W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING at the root composite and the refuted initial-entry check for transition:line:19, this is exact negative evidence for NL3. (2) The event 'Power_On' and 'Enter_Autonomous_Mode' both have declared consumers but zero reachable consumer transitions/states (event_consumer_unreachable diagnostics + verify_facts refuted event-consumer checks), which bears on operational coverage of the power-on entry event even though NL3 is framed as initial_entry not event_consumer_coverage; I derive a distinct event_consumer_coverage obligation for NL3's power-on response semantics. (3) NL5-TERM-1 requires stable termination on power off; tr_0006/transition:line:21 HumanDriving->[*] exists and is reachable_from_initial=true, and root final state is not re-entered further (no continuation from '[*]' root final), so this contract appears satisfied and is omitted. (4) NL4.2-DERIVED reachability of AutoFinal is satisfied (state:AutoFinal:line:11 reachable_from_initial=true via AutoInitial->AutoFinal), so omitted. (5) Cross-wrapper: Autonomous->HumanDriving transition (line 18) requires guard R45RouteToken==5 which is only ever set by the AutoFinal/AutoInitial->[*] internal effects; this looks operationally consistent, not flagged separately here since NL4.2-END-1 is a different lens's endpoint-existence contract already covered by structural lens; I focus on the deeper behavioral defect: the internal exit-to-[*] transitions from AutoInitial and AutoFinal (lines 14,15) target the composite's own internal final pseudostate, which per the fcstm text is consumed by the enclosing Autonomous->HumanDriving guarded transition (R45RouteToken==5), forming the actual NL4.2 relation; this is a distinct behavioral binding worth noting via semantic_bindings rather than a new candidate since the endpoint issue is already the structural lens's contract.

decisions.basis: candidate.observed/basis fields (verify_facts, reference_inspection_facts, inspection_equivalent_facts) and binding.source_refs/element_refs for obligation 0040:r3:i0 in the supplied correction dossier.
decisions.reason: The NL clause 'when power on, the system turn into human driving mode' (NL3) is bound to the exact root initial edge transition:line:19 ([*] -> HumanDriving, trigger Power_On). verify_facts deterministically refutes this edge as an unconditional initial-entry candidate (status=refuted, has_trigger=true), and reference_inspection_facts flags W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING for the root composite, establishing that no unconditional default entry exists as authored. This is exact negative evidence for the initial_entry property, so grounding is established. However, because the sole authored edge exactly matches the sole named NL event (Power_On), a competent alternative reading remains that the author intended this event-triggered edge itself to serve as the entry mechanism (an event-conditioned default rather than a truly unconditional one), which is a second semantic reading compatible with the same facts and is preserved as a surviving undercutting defeater rather than resolved outright.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The PlantUML source explicitly writes '[*] --> HumanDriving : Power On', which is the only root-level initial edge into HumanDriving and directly encodes the NL's own power-on event; under this reading the edge is an intentionally event-gated single initial transition (a normal single-trigger initial edge) rather than a malformed conditional edge, since no other competing unconditional edge or trigger-free alternative is present in the closed model.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL-CONTRACT-NL3-INIT-1 requires an unconditional root/initial pseudostate edge establishing HumanDrivingMode as the default first-entered state on power-on.

decisions.basis: candidate.observed/basis fields (fcstm_model transitions, smt_facts guard, exact_source_inventory, working_contract source_trace) and binding.element_refs/source_refs for obligation 0040:r3:i1 in the supplied correction dossier.
decisions.reason: The NL clause requires transit to HumanDrivingMode from AutonomousMode/AutoFinal on the disjunctive trigger. decisions.strongest_defeater: The working_contract source_trace positively maps tr_0005 as a single macro root spanning the three segments at lines 14, 15, and 18 (compiler:transition_segment:tr_0005:segment:1/2/3), so the fragmented realization (AutoInitial->[*], AutoFinal->[*], Autonomous->HumanDriving) may be read as one authorized compiler-owned macro-closure rendering of the single declared NL transition rather than a genuinely missing or mistargeted endpoint relation.

decisions.basis: candidate.observed/basis fields (smt_facts formula guard:transition:line:18, inspection_equivalent_facts, exact_source_inventory) for obligation 0040:r3:i2 in the supplied correction dossier.

decisions.basis: candidate.observed/basis fields (inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers, diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE, verify_facts.non_proved) for obligation 0040:r3:i4 in the supplied correction dossier.

decisions.strongest_defeater: HumanDriving is nonetheless flagged reachable_from_initial=true in the model's flattened global reachability closure (as distinct from this narrow per-event consumer computation), so a competent alternative reading is that the operational power-on response is still achieved through some other code path not captured by the local event-consumer reachability check, even though this specific consumer edge's local reachability flag is false.

decisions.reason: The NL clause requires transit to HumanDrivingMode from AutonomousMode/AutoFinal on the disjunctive trigger. The exact model facts show this relation realized across three separate transitions (line 14, 15, 18) rather than one coherent edge, with the final consuming edge (line 18) using an opaque token guard rather than the literal disjunctive condition. This fragmentation and the endpoint-continuity gap is established negative evidence for the transition_endpoints property. The candidate itself identifies a competent second reading -- that the macro/token relay is a legitimate compiler-owned decomposition of one PlantUML transition into pyfcstm's segment structure -- which is a second semantic reading compatible with the same underlying facts and constitutes a surviving undercutting defeater, since the macro-closure question (whether this decomposition is an authorized rendering) is not resolved by the supplied facts alone.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The working_contract source_trace positively maps tr_0005 as a single macro root spanning the three segments at lines 14, 15, and 18 (compiler:transition_segment:tr_0005:segment:1/2/3), so the fragmented realization (AutoInitial->[*], AutoFinal->[*], Autonomous->HumanDriving) may be read as one authorized compiler-owned macro-closure rendering of the single declared NL transition rather than a genuinely missing or mistargeted endpoint relation.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL-CONTRACT-NL4.2-END-1 requires a transition from AutonomousMode (or AutoFinal) to HumanDrivingMode guarded/triggered by the disjunctive condition 'human_steering_cmd || brake_pressed || in (AutoFinal)'.

decisions.basis: candidate.observed/basis fields (smt_facts formula guard:transition:line:18, inspection_equivalent_facts, exact_source_inventory) for obligation 0040:r3:i2 in the supplied correction dossier.
decisions.reason: The NL/contract requires the consuming Autonomous->HumanDriving edge to carry the disjunctive guard. The exact smt_facts formula for transition:line:18 shows guard='R45RouteToken == 5' with empty triggers, while the disjunctive predicate appears only as an event name upstream at lines 14/15 -- this is exact evidence that the literal guard on the state-changing edge is an opaque internal proxy, not the declared condition, establishing the guard-property violation. The candidate's own strongest_rebuttal -- that this is a compiler-owned macro decomposition where the token is an implementation artifact equivalent to the source condition -- is a second competent reading not excluded by the supplied facts (no equivalence proof or refutation of that macro reading is supplied), so it survives as an undercutting defeater rather than being defeated outright.
decisions.strongest_defeater: Under the protected-macro discipline, the entire tr_0005 macro (segments at lines 14, 15, 18) may be evaluated as a single unit where the disjunctive event triggers an internal route and the R45RouteToken==5 guard is merely a compiler-introduced implementation artifact of splitting one PlantUML transition into pyfcstm's required event+guard segments, making the token guard a realization detail rather than a directly authored, semantically distinct guard violation.
decisions.violated_obligation: The transition that delivers control from AutonomousMode to HumanDrivingMode must carry a guard/trigger equivalent to the disjunctive predicate human_steering_cmd || brake_pressed || in (AutoFinal).

decisions.basis: candidate.observed/basis fields (inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions, verify_facts.non_proved, reference_inspection_facts.diagnostics) and binding.element_refs for obligation 0040:r3:i3 in the supplied correction dossier.
decisions.reason: The obligation requires the Power_On-triggered root edge (transition:line:19) to attributably establish first entry into HumanDriving. The exact facts show resolved_source_ref=null and reachable_from_initial=false for this specific edge, and verify_facts independently refutes it as an initial-entry candidate; reference_inspection_facts corroborates with the W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING diagnostic. This is established negative evidence that the specific edge does not exactly satisfy the attributable initial-entry property. However, HumanDriving is globally reachable_from_initial=true per the flattened inspection facts, and since it is the sole candidate edge, a competent alternative reading is that the deterministic backend's global reachability closure (rather than this specific edge-level attribution flag) should govern satisfaction of the contract -- a second reading compatible with the same facts that is not excluded by the supplied dossier, so it survives as an undercutting defeater.
decisions.strongest_defeater: inspection_equivalent_facts.reachable_state_refs flattens HumanDriving as reachable_from_initial=true, and since no competing initial edge into HumanDriving exists in the closed model, the deterministic backend could treat this sole root initial edge as the canonical (attributable) entry mechanism regardless of the local refuted-check/resolved_source_ref=null flags, which pertain to a stricter per-edge attribution test rather than global reachability.
decisions.violated_obligation: The exact root/initial pseudostate edge triggered by Power_On must establish the system's effective, attributable first entry into HumanDriving.

decisions.basis: candidate.observed/basis fields (inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers, diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE, verify_facts.non_proved) for obligation 0040:r3:i4 in the supplied correction dossier.
decisions.reason: NL3 requires the power-on stimulus to produce actual reachable behavior (entry to HumanDriving), not merely a declared consumer edge. The exact deterministic facts show inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers for Power_On has consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:19] but reachable_consumer_state_refs=[] and reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[], with the EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostic explicitly stating consumers exist but none is reachable from a top-level initial entry, and verify_facts confirms this is refuted. This is a complete, exact negative finding on the reachable-consumer coverage property (a different, stronger property than mere declaration), establishing the violation per the property-preserving protocol (a declared consumer does not rebut a reachable-consumer requirement). The candidate's own rebuttal -- that HumanDriving might be reached via a different, uncaptured path per the global reachability closure -- is a second reading not excluded by the supplied per-event consumer facts, so it survives as an undercutting defeater rather than being defeated.
decisions.strongest_defeater: HumanDriving is nonetheless flagged reachable_from_initial=true in the model's flattened global reachability closure (as distinct from this narrow per-event consumer computation), so a competent alternative reading is that the operational power-on response is still achieved through some other code path not captured by the local event-consumer reachability check, even though this specific consumer edge's local reachability flag is false.
decisions.violated_obligation: The Power_On event's response (entry into HumanDriving) must be reachable from the model's top-level initial entry within the required operating scope, not merely declared as a consumer edge.
